rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the highest-priority need is to establish a reliable performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest and cheapest configuration in the search space: it uses the most basic RNA encoder (PCA), a single profile (no aggregation needed), and no image modality. This gives a fast, low-variance reference point. All subsequent experiments—testing multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders (scVI, scGPT), image modality, and multimodal fusion—can be interpreted relative to this floor. Starting here maximizes information per experiment: if it performs well, we know the task is tractable with minimal machinery; if it underperforms, we immediately learn which axis (encoder quality, multi-profile aggregation, or image modality) to explore next. Under a limited budget, spending the first slot on the cheapest, most interpretable baseline is the most efficient use of resources.

We have only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), giving us essentially no information about whether the image modality contributes useful signal. The most critical uncertainty to resolve before committing budget to multimodal or encoder variations is whether image features alone are informative for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is a clean, single-variable comparison against our existing RNA-only baseline: it isolates the image modality's contribution using a standard, well-understood encoder. If image-only accuracy is comparable to RNA-only (~48%), it suggests neither modality is sufficient alone and multimodal fusion is essential. If image-only is substantially higher, it redirects our search toward image encoders and multimodal fusion strategies. If substantially lower, it confirms RNA as the primary signal and justifies focusing on RNA encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most fundamental design axis (modality) before we spend budget on more complex multimodal or encoder configurations.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA-2000) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) is much weaker at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We have no information on whether multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) improves over singleprofile for the RNA modality. This experiment (config_002) is a clean, single-variable comparison against config_001—only the profile setting changes from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation—directly isolating the effect of multi-profile aggregation. If multiprofile helps, it validates investing in transformer aggregation (config_003) and better encoders with multiprofile; if it does not, we avoid wasting budget on all multiprofile variants. Under a tight budget, this controlled A/B test on our strongest modality maximally reduces uncertainty about a core architectural choice before committing to more complex multimodal or encoder variants.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a strong +10.5pp gain over config_001 (singleprofile, 0.485), confirming multiprofile is highly beneficial. However, we have not yet tested transformer aggregation, leaving a critical architectural question unresolved. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for multiprofile RNA? config_003 is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002 (only aggregation changes). Why this is the best next step: The aggregation choice will propagate into every subsequent multimodal experiment (configs 018-051 all require an aggregation decision). Resolving this now with a controlled, low-cost RNA-only experiment reduces uncertainty about a foundational design choice before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations. It is the highest-information-per-experiment choice given the current sparse evidence.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool (config_002, acc=0.591) is the strongest configuration so far, while image-only resnet50 (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak in isolation. The central open question for a multimodal profiling study is whether the weak image signal carries complementary morphological information that, when fused with the strong RNA signal, improves over RNA alone. This experiment (config_018: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) directly tests that question by taking the best-validated RNA pipeline and adding the image branch with the simplest fusion (concat). If it significantly beats 0.591, it confirms multimodal value and justifies further fusion/image-encoder exploration; if it does not, it tells us to focus remaining budget on RNA encoder alternatives (scvi, scgpt) rather than image fusion. This is the highest-information single experiment because its outcome bifurcates the entire remaining search space.

Evidence: The best-performing config so far is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA n2000, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1. RNA carries most of the signal (RNA-only multiprofile avgpool = 0.591 vs image-only = 0.208), and avgpool aggregation clearly beats transformer (0.591 vs 0.519). However, PCA n2000 is the only RNA encoder tested across all experiments. Question: config_030 swaps only the RNA encoder to SCVI n200 (a learned 200-dim latent) while holding every other hyperparameter identical to config_018. This isolates whether a nonlinear, dimensionality-reduced learned representation can match or beat a 2000-dim linear PCA projection. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is the highest-leverage untested design axis because RNA dominates the signal. If SCVI n200 outperforms PCA n2000, it opens a productive direction across all fusion/image-encoder variants; if it underperforms, we confirm PCA's robustness and can redirect budget toward image encoder or fusion strategy. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty with minimal confounds (one-variable change from the current best).

The current best is config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat; acc=0.632). All multimodal results so far used concat fusion, leaving the fusion strategy entirely unexplored. config_031 is an isolated one-variable change (concat → weighted) from the current best, directly testing whether the way RNA and image features are combined matters. This is a fundamental design decision: if weighted fusion outperforms concat, it can be applied across all multimodal configurations to improve performance; if it is equivalent or worse, we can rule out that axis and focus budget on image encoder or aggregation choices. Under a limited budget, this clean A/B comparison maximizes information gain about a high-impact, currently untested design dimension.

The current best (config_031: scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.678) shows that weighted fusion and multiprofile aggregation are strong contributors. However, the image encoder (ResNet50) performed very poorly in isolation (config_010: acc=0.208), raising the question of whether the image modality's contribution in the multimodal setting is bottlenecked by encoder capacity. Config_037 is a clean, single-variable extension of config_031 that swaps ResNet50 for the much stronger Imagenet ViT-L while keeping all other settings identical (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This directly tests whether upgrading the image encoder unlocks additional signal that ResNet50 cannot capture. If performance improves meaningfully, the image encoder becomes a key lever for further gains; if not, we can confidently rule out image-encoder quality as a bottleneck and redirect budget toward RNA encoder (scgpt) or fusion/aggregation refinements. Under a limited budget, this experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about one of the two modalities' contribution while staying anchored to the current best configuration.

Evidence: The current best (config_037, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, 0.706 acc) establishes a strong multimodal configuration, and scvi_n200 has shown a modest edge over pca_n2000. However, the scgpt RNA encoder is completely untested across all experiments, representing the largest remaining uncertainty in the design space. Question: config_049 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) isolates the RNA encoder as the only variable changed from the current best, directly testing whether scgpt can match or exceed scvi_n200 in the strongest known multimodal context. Why this is the best use of the next experiment: With a limited budget, testing an entirely unexplored encoder in the best-known configuration provides the highest information gain per experiment—either confirming scvi_n200 as the optimal RNA encoder (reducing search space) or revealing a superior alternative that could further improve performance. The other untested dimensions (transformer aggregation, singleprofile) already have moderate negative evidence from prior runs, making them lower-priority uncertainties compared to the completely unknown scgpt performance.

The current best is config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.706). In the RNA-only setting, avgpool clearly outperformed transformer (0.591 vs 0.519), but that comparison was made without a strong image encoder. In the multimodal setting, the interaction between aggregation strategy and the VIT image features is untested. Config_039 is a single-variable extension of the best configuration, swapping avgpool for transformer while keeping all other settings identical. This directly tests whether transformer aggregation can better capture cross-profile and cross-modal interactions when paired with the richer VIT image representations. If it improves, we identify a new best; if it does not, we confirm avgpool as the optimal aggregation and can focus remaining budget on other dimensions. Under a limited budget, this is the highest-information experiment because it resolves uncertainty on the last unexplored design axis of the current best configuration without introducing multiple confounding changes.
